active_rules.description: Firewall zone drifting is enabled, which may lead to unexpected network access.
active_rules.summary: Firewall zone drifting is enabled, which may lead to unexpected network access.
active_rules.generic: When firewall zone drifting is enabled, network interfaces may move between zones unexpectedly, potentially exposing services to untrusted networks.
active_rules.reason: This host has firewalld configured with AllowZoneDrifting=yes, which is deprecated and may cause unexpected network access patterns.

resolution_set.resolution: Red Hat recommends setting AllowZoneDrifting=no in /etc/firewalld/firewalld.conf and restarting the firewalld service.

active_rules.description: The /etc/ssh/sshd_config file has permissions that are more permissive than recommended.
active_rules.summary: The /etc/ssh/sshd_config file has permissions that are more permissive than recommended.
active_rules.generic: The sshd_config file should have restrictive permissions to prevent unauthorized users from reading or modifying the SSH server configuration.
active_rules.reason: This host has /etc/ssh/sshd_config with permissions 0644, which is more permissive than the recommended 0600.
active_rules.more_info: For more information, see the RHEL Security Guide section on SSH hardening.

resolution_set.resolution: Red Hat recommends setting the permissions of /etc/ssh/sshd_config to 0600 by running: chmod 0600 /etc/ssh/sshd_config

active_rules.description: kernel.panic_on_oops is enabled, which may cause unnecessary system reboots.
active_rules.summary: kernel.panic_on_oops is enabled, which may cause unnecessary system reboots.
active_rules.generic: When kernel.panic_on_oops is enabled, any kernel oops will cause a full system panic and reboot, which may result in unnecessary downtime for recoverable errors.
active_rules.reason: This host has kernel.panic_on_oops set to 1. Kernel oops events that would normally be recoverable will instead trigger a full system panic and reboot.

resolution_set.resolution: Red Hat recommends setting kernel.panic_on_oops=0 via sysctl. Add kernel.panic_on_oops=0 to /etc/sysctl.d/99-custom.conf and run sysctl -p.
